claims.statement: The HO-4 2013-07 edition is superseded by HO-4 2021-10 for policies effective on or after 2021-10-01, while 2013-07 remains applicable to policies written under that edition; the two forms have effective dates 2013-07-01 and 2021-10-01 respectively.

Both HO-4 editions expressly provide no Coverage A, so the policy does not insure the dwelling or building property under Coverage A; Coverage D and some additional-coverages provisions nevertheless reference a Coverage A limit and must not be converted into assumed dwelling coverage.

HO-4 organizes property protection through Coverage B Other Structures, Coverage C Personal Property, and Coverage D Loss of Use, while Section I Coverage E contains Additional Coverages and Section II Coverage E and Coverage F provide Personal Liability and Medical Payments to Others.

The Coverage B settlement wording changed between editions: 2013-07 uses actual cash value when repair or replacement is not completed and permits repair, rebuilding, or replacement, while 2021-10 limits payment to the lesser of repair or replacement cost, actual cash value, or the Coverage B limit and permits taking paid-for property at the value paid.

The 2021-10 Coverage C special limits increased from 2013-07 for electronic apparatus in a motor vehicle, money and precious metals, theft of jewelry/watches/precious stones, theft of firearms, watercraft, and business property on the residence premises; the silverware limit remained $2,500 in both editions.

Coverage D covers qualifying additional living expense, fair rental value, and civil-authority loss of use, subject to records, mitigation, and covered-loss conditions; its stated limit changed from 30% of the Coverage A limit in 2013-07 to 40% in 2021-10.

The HO-4 base forms exclude major water boundaries including flood/surface water, subsurface water, sewer or drain backup, sump overflow or discharge, and continuous or repeated seepage or leakage, along with deterioration and fungi/rot/bacteria conditions; covered sudden and accidental discharge is subject to the edition's peril wording and exclusions.

Both editions impose material post-loss duties including notice, protection and retention of damaged property, records and inventory, examination under oath, sworn proof of loss within 60 days after request, cooperation, disclosure of other insurance, and preservation of recovery rights; appraisal determines amount of loss rather than coverage. The 2013-07 form makes payment due within 60 days after agreement, a binding appraisal award, or final judgment, while 2021-10 states payment within 60 days after agreement on the amount of loss, subject to applicable conditions.

Section II Coverage E pays covered occurrence-based bodily-injury or property-damage liability and provides a defense for a covered suit until the applicable liability limit is exhausted; Coverage F pays qualifying medical expenses to persons other than insureds without regard to fault, generally for expenses incurred within three years of the accident, subject to edition-specific exclusions.

HO 04 92 Water Backup — Tenants (2019-03) writes back limited direct-physical-loss coverage for covered personal property caused by defined water backup, subject to a $2,500 limit and $250 deductible, while preserving other policy exclusions and not creating coverage for otherwise ineligible property.

HO 04 27 Limited Water Damage Coverage (2016-05) modifies HO-4 water-damage terms by covering specified sudden and accidental discharge, overflow, breakage, or freezing events and preserves exclusions for repeated seepage, sewer/drain/sump backup, subsurface water, flood, fungi/rot/bacteria, and failed diversion systems; its stated limits include $2,500 for backup/sump overflow and $5,000 for fungi, wet or dry rot, or bacteria.

The seeded HO 04 61 Scheduled Personal Property editions and HO 04 65 Coverage C Increased Special Limits edition identify their line as HO-3 rather than HO-4, so they should not be applied as HO-4 endorsements without an applicable attachment or schedule establishing that use.

The 2021-10 filing memorandum is an interpretive filing map describing revisions to deductible administration, policy continuation, mold wording, claim-handling authority, Coverage D and special-limit presentation, post-loss conditions, and Section II liability wording; it does not itself grant coverage, so the governing form, declarations, and attached endorsements control if wording differs.

The editions present the named-peril grant differently: 2013-07 uses a separate Perils Insured Against section requiring direct physical loss caused by a listed named peril, while 2021-10 embeds covered-peril provisions in Coverage C and adds edition-specific location, water, system, and resulting-loss qualifications; the applicable edition's exact peril clause controls.

Coverage C settlement differs by edition: 2013-07 determines value at the time of loss, permits depreciation for actual cash value, and allows repair, replacement, or payment, while 2021-10 limits payment to the amount needed to repair or replace with like kind and quality, permits actual-cash-value depreciation, addresses pairs, sets, and unavailable parts, and permits taking damaged property at agreed or appraised value.

The Section II additional property-damage coverage increased from a $1,000 maximum in 2013-07 to a $1,500 maximum in 2021-10; 2013-07 requires the damaged property to be in the care of a person other than an insured, while 2021-10 makes payment available regardless of legal liability and retains edition-specific property relationship exclusions and exceptions.

For a tenant, Section II liability does not insure the tenant's own contents as liability property damage or automatically cover the landlord's dwelling: the editions exclude property owned by, rented to, occupied by, used by, or in the care of an insured, with 2021-10 expressly preserving stated fire, smoke, or explosion exceptions for certain rented, occupied, or loaned property.

Both base HO-4 editions can cover sudden accidental water discharge or overflow damage to qualifying personal property while excluding the dwelling, building systems, and source-system property under their base wording; water backup, flood or surface water, subsurface water, gradual seepage, and fungi or rot require the edition-specific exclusions and any attached endorsement to be analyzed separately.
